title: Market, format version 1
description: A play-money question about the future that settles itself from real data: when it closes, settlement reads its subject's data slot and pays out with no one touching it. The exact questions are settled in PLAN.md step 3.2.

format.description: Says this record is a market, in format version 1.

question.description: The question people bet on, as shown.

subject.description: What the market is about. Its data slot settles the market, in the way the shared list describes.

categories.description: The categories whose news shows alongside the market.

kind.description: yes_no: people buy Yes or No (a price subject). multiple_choice: several outcomes, exactly one of which wins (a ranking or match subject).

outcomes.description: The possible outcomes. Required for multiple_choice, and only there. At most one is the catch-all.

threshold.description: For a price subject: Yes wins if the settlement price is above this, in US dollars. Required there, and only there.

match_ref.description: For a match subject: which match, by the code its readings use. Required there, and only there.

closes_at.description: When betting stops. Settlement reads the data slot from this time.

state.description: upcoming: not open yet. open: taking bets. closed: betting has stopped and settlement waits for the data. settled: paid out. void: cancelled, with every bet returned.

result.description: What won: yes or no, or the winning outcome's code. Only when the state is settled.

void_reason.description: Why the market was cancelled, in our own words. Only when the state is void.

settled_at.description: When it was settled or cancelled. Only when the state is settled or void.

updated_at.description: When anything about the market last changed.

code.description: The outcome's code, which the result names if it wins. Unique within the market.

reading_value.description: What the subject's data says when this outcome wins: a model's name as the ranking gives it, or a match result (home, away, draw or no_result).

otherwise.description: Marks the catch-all outcome (such as "Another model"), which wins when no other outcome's reading_value matches.
